note: Display labels for DEC worlds (named graphs). The DEC type, governing agent and content are read from the knowledge graph; this file only adds human-readable titles ('title') and a short phrase usable after a verb ('short').

reality.title: Reality
reality.desc: What is true in the story: the narrated facts plus Holmes's solution, which the story accepts (DEC reality).

shared.title: Shared background
shared.desc: Vocabulary and rules everyone shares (e.g. a journey cannot be both actual and pretended).

mary_D1.title: Mary's beliefs
mary_D1.desc: What Mary believes when she visits Baker Street. No later scene shows her again.

holmes_reconstruction.title: Holmes's solution
holmes_reconstruction.desc: Holmes's explanation of the case. The story accepts it: Windibank half-admits it and the firm's letter confirms it.

holmes_mother.title: Holmes: the mother helped
holmes_mother.desc: Holmes's claim that the mother was in on it, supported only by Windibank's “we”.

holmes_motive.title: Holmes: the motive
holmes_motive.desc: Holmes's explanation of why: keeping the daughter's income.

holmes_same_machine.title: Holmes: the same typewriter
holmes_same_machine.desc: “No two of them write exactly alike”: the same defects mean the same machine.

holmes_prediction.title: Holmes's prediction
holmes_prediction.desc: “If I tell her she will not believe me”: what Holmes expects Mary would do.

watson_hyp.title: Watson's guess
watson_hyp.desc: The signature was typed so that it could be denied in a breach-of-promise case. Holmes rejects it.

windibank_beliefs.title: Windibank's beliefs
windibank_beliefs.desc: What Windibank knows while playing himself and Hosmer. The story never states them: the editors attribute them from Holmes's solution.

v_hosmer_cashier.title: Hosmer: “a cashier in Leadenhall Street”
v_hosmer_cashier.desc: How Hosmer described himself, as Mary reports it.

v_mary_france.title: Mary: “father went to France”
v_mary_france.desc: What Mary tells Holmes about her stepfather's journey.

v_windibank_reassure.title: Windibank: “something happened to him”
v_windibank_reassure.desc: Reported by Mary: “he seemed to think, with me, that something had happened”.

v_windibank_delighted.title: Windibank: “I am delighted to hear it”
v_windibank_delighted.desc: His reply when Holmes says he will find Hosmer Angel.

v_windibank_machine.title: Windibank: “We do all our correspondence with this machine”
v_windibank_machine.desc: What he admits about the office typewriter.

v_windibank_denial.title: Windibank: “this sort of fantastic talk”
v_windibank_denial.desc: His answer when Holmes shows that the letters from Hosmer have the same typing defects as his own: he dismisses it and speaks of Hosmer Angel as another man (“If you can catch the man, catch him”). Implied: he is not Hosmer Angel.

h_author_other.title: What-if: another clerk typed the letters
h_author_other.desc: Not in the story. The editors added it to test what the typewriter evidence alone can prove.

reality.title: Reality (so far)
reality.desc: What a reader can take as true at this point of the story.

w01.title: Mary's beliefs
w01.desc: Mary's beliefs as she tells them to Holmes.

w05.title: Watson's guess
w05.desc: The typed signature as a breach-of-promise trick.

w07.title: Windibank: “fantastic talk”
w07.desc: Said to Holmes, about the letters. Implied: he is not Hosmer Angel.

w10.title: Holmes's solution
w10.desc: Stated at the unmasking, and accepted from that point on.

w20.title: Reader's guess: Hosmer is the stepfather
w20.desc: A guess of the simulated first-time reader.

w21.title: Reader's guess: something happened to him
w21.desc: Mary's view, taken as a guess.

w22.title: Holmes: the same typewriter
w22.desc: The same defects mean the same machine.

w23.title: Reader's guess: the stepfather typed the letters
w23.desc: A guess about who typed them.

w24.title: What-if: another clerk typed them
w24.desc: Not in the story: a test alternative.
